_comment: World Health Organization, World Malaria Report 2025: global map of malaria status in 2024, as attached to Taiwan CDC's 瘧疾預防用藥 page (瘧疾感染風險地圖). Digitised country by country from the image (registration of world.json onto the map, majority colour inside each country), then checked by eye on enlarged crops where borders are tight or countries are small, and cross-checked against WHO's list of countries and territories certified malaria-free (source.certified_list, read 2026-11-06): 'certified' is exactly the countries WHO certified in 2000 or later (Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar, read as green on the small image, are on WHO's list from before / outside that period and are 'no malaria'). Syria reads in the certified colour on the image but is not on WHO's certification list; WHO gives it malaria-free status (no indigenous cases since 2005; refs.SY), so it is classed with the countries with zero indigenous cases for 3+ years. Countries not listed are white on the map (no malaria). Re-check when CDC replaces the image or WHO certifies another country.

source.title: World Malaria Report 2025 — countries by malaria status, 2024

notes.MY: Malaysia has a significant number of indigenous malaria cases caused by Plasmodium knowlesi infection; zero indigenous cases of human Plasmodium species for the seventh consecutive year in 2024.
notes.SA: Zero indigenous cases for the fourth consecutive year in 2024.
notes.BT: Zero indigenous cases for the third consecutive year in 2024, ending the malaria epidemic.
notes.SY: Not on WHO's list of countries certified malaria-free; WHO gives the Syrian Arab Republic malaria-free status (no indigenous cases since 2005). Shown in the certified colour on the WHO map image.
